key_insight: Doc-to-Atom extends context distillation from one monolithic adapter per document to a composable set of smaller "memory atoms," enabling more flexible and query-specific use of long-context information. In simple terms, it learns to compile a document into reusable pieces that can be recombined at inference time.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the high memory and compute cost of long-context inference in LLMs, especially when document information must be reused across many queries. It also addresses the limitation of generating a single adapter for an entire document, which can be too coarse for different questions.
method: Compress a document into multiple smaller memory atoms instead of one large adapter.
Learn a compiler-like mechanism that composes the right atoms for each query.
Use these atoms to amortize context distillation in a single forward pass, reducing reliance on full attention over long inputs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this can make long-document reasoning faster and more memory-efficient without sacrificing adaptability across different queries. It is especially useful for retrieval-heavy workflows, document QA, and scenarios where the same context must support many downstream questions.
